basics.name: Zachary Newsom
basics.label: Electrical Engineer, Indie Game Developer
basics.summary: BS in Electrical Engineering, interested in RF, audio signal processing, PCB design, power electronics, and power system planning. 8+ years experience in indie game development, with a focus on graphics programming and innovative gameplay mechanics.

work.name: Avista Utilities
work.summary: Wrote reports, performed studies and learned a lot about the economic and technical complexities that go into planning for future electricity demand on Avista's Eastern WA/North ID section of the grid.
highlights: Wrote system upgrade studies that took into account–amongst other factors–contingency analyses, load growth projections, temperature-dependent system current limits (i.e. FERC order 881) and renewable resource integration.
Performed transmission and distribution level powerflow analysis with PowerWorld and Synergi.
Created capacity-need estimates for various residential development types.
Interfaced with substation, protection, and operations teams. Got a broad overview of the operation of a power utility.

work.name: WSU Systems-on-Chip Lab / Boeing (sponsor)
work.summary: Team of four tasked with the design, modeling, and testing of a 40–44 GHz FMCW radar system optimized for cryogenic environments. Used the ICE-T cryogenics electronics test-bed.
highlights: Sole PCB drafter/designer. Used Altium and fabricated via PCBway.
Developed MATLAB/Simulink RADAR simulations and DSP models.
Contributed to design of high-gain PCB patch antenna array via ADS and Altium.
Integrated commercial RFSoC (ZCU111) for signal generation/processing.

Tested and characterized indidual commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) electronic components with custom PCBs at cryogenic temperatures (down to 4K) to evaluate performance gains from thermal noise reduction and find their functional breakdown temperature.

Designed component-testing circuits and created custom PCBs for characterizing thin film resistors, various dielectric SMD capacitors (including NP0/C0G), GanFETs (EPC-xxx), voltage regulators (LT6654), precision low-noise op-amps (LMP2022), 4-channel CMOS switches (TMUX1574), matched BJT pairs (DMMT3904W), current monitors (ZXCT1009F) and more.

work.name: Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories
work.summary: Worked in the protective relay/recloser controls manufacturing support department. Learned a lot about the process engineering that goes into a complex manufacturing floor.
highlights: Supported the manufacturing and testing of SEL-651R Recloser and SEL-2431 Voltage Regulator controls–as well as adjacent products, namely cables and harnesses.
Designed and maintained test cabinets and custom scripts for technicians to functionally test products before shipping. Fulfilled station support requests.
Learned to troubleshoot products at cabinet and board level as an occassional production troubleshooting technician.

Programmed custom instrument control code, for our in-house manufacturing test scripting language, that implemented externally-designed cable/harness testers (CAMI Research) as scriptable instruments. Learned about COM and build systems, created extensive documentation, implemented use on the manufacturing floor.

work.name: Game Development Club at WSU
work.summary: Founded and grew WSU's Game Development Club, teaching workshops and leading game jams.
highlights: Hosted yearly game jams with 100+ participants
Taught pixel art, 3D art, coding, and game design
Programmed indie games in Unity, Godot, and C++/OpenGL

work.name: Crimson Robotics (WSU BattleBots Team)
work.summary: Led electrical and software efforts on combat robotics projects.
highlights: Designed custom PCBs for battery monitoring, motherboard, and telemetry
Configured FOC-based ESCs and rated components
Used SolidWorks for robot modeling
